title: Perfluorooctanoic acid and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid induce immunotoxicity through the NF-kappaB pathway in black-spotted frog (Rana nigromaculata).
authors: Liu, Zhiquan; Lin, Huikang; Zheng, Yueyue; Feng, Yixuan; Shi, Chaoli; Zhu, Ruoxin; Shen, Xingyao; Han, Yu; Zhang, Hangjun; Zhong, Yuchi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PFOA/PFOS通过NF-kappaB通路诱导青蛙免疫毒性，含分子对接但非TF-DNA互作核心，方法简单且对象为环境毒理，与课题关联有限。
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) are widely detected in the environment and wild animals, thus posing a threat to wildlife and public health; however, knowledge about their immunotoxicity and the underlying mechanism remains limited. In the present study, male black-spotted frogs (Rana nigromaculata) were exposed to environmentally relevant concentrations (0, 1, and 10 mug/L) of PFOA or PFOS for 21 days; subsequently, biochemical analysis, molecular docking, and gene expression determination were conducted. The results indicated that exposure to 10 mug/L PFOA decreased the serum levels of immunoglobulin A. PFOS exposure significantly increased the hepatic levels of interleukin-1beta, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interferon-gamma, and nitric oxide; but PFOA significantly increased the levels of only tumor necrosis factor-alpha. Furthermore, PFOA and PFOS exposure significantly decreased the activity of inducible nitric oxide synthase and total nitric oxide synthase. IBRv2 analysis indicated that PFOA and PFOS had a similar effect on these immune indicators, but PFOS was more toxic than PFOA. Molecular docking revealed that PFOA and PFOS can bind to nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) by forming stable hydrogen bonds. PFOA and PFOS exposure upregulated the gene expression of NF-kappaB and its downstream genes. Significant correlations between the expression of genes involved in the NF-kappaB pathway and immune-related indicators suggests that PFOA- and PFOS-induced immunotoxicity was associated with the activation of NF-kappaB. Our findings provide novel insights into the potential role of NF-kappaB in immunotoxicity induced by PFOA and PFOS in frogs.
abstract_zh: 全氟辛酸（PFOA）和全氟辛烷磺酸（PFOS）在环境和野生动物中广泛检出，从而对野生动物和公共健康构成威胁；然而，关于其免疫毒性及潜在机制的知识仍然有限。在本研究中，雄性黑斑蛙（Rana nigromaculata）暴露于环境相关浓度（0、1和10 μg/L）的PFOA或PFOS 21天；随后，进行了生化分析、分子对接和基因表达测定。结果表明，暴露于10 μg/L PFOA降低了血清中免疫球蛋白A的水平。PFOS暴露显著增加了肝脏中白细胞介素-1β、白细胞介素-6、肿瘤坏死因子-α、干扰素-γ和一氧化氮的水平；但PFOA仅显著增加了肿瘤坏死因子-α的水平。此外，PFOA和PFOS暴露显著降低了诱导型一氧化氮合酶和总一氧化氮合酶的活性。IBRv2分析表明，PFOA和PFOS对这些免疫指标具有相似的影响，但PFOS的毒性大于PFOA。分子对接揭示，PFOA和PFOS可通过形成稳定的氢键与核因子-κB（NF-κB）结合。PFOA和PFOS暴露上调了NF-κB及其下游基因的基因表达。NF-κB通路相关基因表达与免疫相关指标之间的显著相关性表明，PFOA和PFOS诱导的免疫毒性与NF-κB的激活相关。我们的发现为NF-κB在PFOA和PFOS诱导的蛙类免疫毒性中的潜在作用提供了新的见解。
